parts.working: M1 product of roots (3/2)(a² − d²) = 3/2 so a² − d² = 1; M1 d² = 9/4 − 1 = 5/4; A1 roots 3/2 ± √5/2.

author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation x³ − 3x² + 4x − 5 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of α³ + β³ + γ³.
parts.working: B1 Σα = 3, Σαβ = 4, αβγ = 5; M1 Σα³ = (Σα)³ − 3ΣαΣαβ + 3αβγ; A1 27 − 36 + 15 = 6.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The matrix M has rows (α, β, γ), (β, γ, α) and (γ, α, β). Show that det M = 3αβγ − (α³ + β³ + γ³) and hence find the value of det M.
parts.working: M1 expand det M = α(γβ − α²) − β(β² − αγ) + γ(αβ − γ²); A1 = 3αβγ − Σα³; A1 15 − 6 = 9.

author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation x³ + 5x² − 3x + 2 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that α²β + α²γ + β²α + β²γ + γ²α + γ²β = (α + β + γ)(αβ + βγ + γα) − 3αβγ, and find its value.
parts.working: M1 expand (Σα)(Σαβ) to get the six terms plus 3αβγ; A1 shown; A1 (−5)(−3) − 3(−2) = 21.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of α/β + β/α + β/γ + γ/β + γ/α + α/γ.
parts.working: M1 common denominator αβγ gives (sum in (a))/αβγ; A1 21/(−2) = −21/2.

author: HomiLabs

stem: The numbers α, β and γ satisfy α + β + γ = 3, α² + β² + γ² = 17 and α³ + β³ + γ³ = 27.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of αβ + βγ + γα and αβγ.
parts.working: M1 Σαβ = ((Σα)² − Σα²)/2 = (9 − 17)/2; A1 −4; M1 Σα³ = (Σα)³ − 3ΣαΣαβ + 3αβγ: 27 = 27 + 36 + 3αβγ; A1 αβγ = −12.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find a cubic equation with integer coefficients whose roots are α, β and γ, and solve it.

author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation x³ + 2x² − x + 3 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of α² + β² + γ².

parts.label: b
parts.text: By writing α + β = −2 − γ, or otherwise, find the value of (α + β)² + (β + γ)² + (γ + α)².

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the value of (α + β)(β + γ)(γ + α).
parts.working: M1 Π(−2 − γ) = −Π(2 + γ) = −(8 + 4Σγ + 2Σαβ + αβγ) with αβγ = −3; A1 5.

check: (lambda a,b,c: a**2-2*b)(Fraction(-2,1),Fraction(-1,1),Fraction(-3,1)) == Fraction(6,1) and (lambda a,b,c: a**2+a**2-2*b)(Fraction(-2,1),Fraction(-1,1),Fraction(-3,1)) == Fraction(10,1) and (lambda a,b,c: a*b-c)(Fraction(-2,1),Fraction(-1,1),Fraction(-3,1)) == Fraction(5,1)
author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation x³ − x + 4 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of α⁴ + β⁴ + γ⁴.
parts.working: M1 α⁴ = α² − 4α from x³ = x − 4; M1 Σα⁴ = Σα² − 4Σα with Σα = 0, Σα² = 0 − 2(−1) = 2; A1 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the equation whose roots are 1/α, 1/β, 1/γ is 4y³ − y² + 1 = 0.
parts.working: M1 substitute x = 1/y: 1/y³ − 1/y + 4 = 0; A1 multiply by y³: 4y³ − y² + 1 = 0.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence find the value of 1/α³ + 1/β³ + 1/γ³.
parts.working: M1 for the new equation Σ1/α = 1/4, Σ1/(αβ) = 0, Π1/α = −1/4; M1 Σy³ = (Σy)³ − 3ΣyΣyz + 3Πy; A1 1/64 − 3/4 = −47/64.

check: Fraction(2)-4*0 == 2 and (lambda a,b,c: a**3-3*a*b+3*c)(Fraction(1,4),Fraction(0,1),Fraction(-1,4)) == Fraction(-47,64) and (lambda a,b,c: (a**2-2*b)-4*a)(Fraction(0,1),Fraction(-1,1),Fraction(-4,1)) == Fraction(2,1)
author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation x⁴ + 2x³ − 3x² + x + 5 = 0 has roots α, β, γ and δ. Let Sₙ = αⁿ + βⁿ + γⁿ + δⁿ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of S₂ and S₃.
parts.working: B1 Σα = −2, Σαβ = −3, Σαβγ = −1, αβγδ = 5; A1 S₂ = 4 + 6 = 10; M1 S₃ = (Σα)³ − 3ΣαΣαβ + 3Σαβγ; A1 −8 − 18 − 3 = −29.

parts.label: b
parts.text: By summing the equation over all four roots after multiplying it by suitable powers of x, find S₄.
parts.working: M1 x⁴ = −2x³ + 3x² − x − 5 so S₄ = −2S₃ + 3S₂ − S₁ − 5S₀ with S₀ = 4, S₁ = −2; M1 substitution: 58 + 30 + 2 − 20; A1 70.

author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation x³ + ax² + bx − 6 = 0, where a and b are real constants, has roots α, β and γ. It is given that α² + β² + γ² = 14 and 1/α + 1/β + 1/γ = 11/6.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that αβ + βγ + γα = 11.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the two possible values of a.
parts.working: M1 (Σα)² = Σα² + 2Σαβ = 14 + 22 = 36; A1 Σα = ±6; A1 a = −Σα so a = −6 or 6.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Given also that all three roots are positive, find the roots.
parts.working: M1 positive roots so Σα = 6, a = −6: x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6 = 0; A1 (x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3) = 0 so 1, 2, 3.

check: Fraction(11,6)*6 == 11 and 14 + 2*11 == 36 and 1+2+3 == 6 and 1**2+2**2+3**2 == 14 and Fraction(1,1)+Fraction(1,2)+Fraction(1,3) == Fraction(11,6) and 1*2*3 == 6
author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation x³ + 3x² − 2x − 1 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the sum of the products in pairs of αβ, βγ and γα is αβγ(α + β + γ), and write down the product αβ·βγ·γα in terms of αβγ.
parts.answer: αβ·βγ + βγ·γα + γα·αβ = αβγ(α + β + γ); product = (αβγ)²
parts.working: B1 each pair product contains αβγ times one root; B1 (αβγ)².

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of (αβ)³ + (βγ)³ + (γα)³.
parts.working: B1 Σα = −3, Σαβ = −2, αβγ = 1; M1 for u = αβ etc: Σu = −2, Σuv = 1 × (−3) = −3, Πu = 1; M1 Σu³ = (Σu)³ − 3ΣuΣuv + 3Πu; A1 −8 − 18 + 3 = −23.

author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation x³ − 2x² + 3x − 4 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of α² + β² + γ² and α²β² + β²γ² + γ²α².
parts.answer: α² + β² + γ² = −2, α²β² + β²γ² + γ²α² = −7

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of (α² + 1)(β² + 1)(γ² + 1).
parts.working: M1 expand: α²β²γ² + Σα²β² + Σα² + 1; A1 16 − 7 − 2 + 1 = 8.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Verify your answer to part (b) by considering p(i)p(−i), where p(x) = x³ − 2x² + 3x − 4 and i² = −1.

author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation x³ − 4x + 1 = 0 has roots α, β and γ. Let Sₙ = αⁿ + βⁿ + γⁿ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that S₍ₙ₊₃₎ = 4S₍ₙ₊₁₎ − Sₙ.
parts.working: M1 multiply α³ = 4α − 1 by αⁿ; A1 sum over α, β, γ.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the values of S₂, S₃ and S₅.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence find the value of α²(β³ + γ³) + β²(γ³ + α³) + γ²(α³ + β³).
parts.working: M1 expression = S₂S₃ − S₅; A1 8(−3) − (−20) = −4.

author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation x⁴ + x² + 2x + 6 = 0 has roots α, β, γ and δ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of α² + β² + γ² + δ² and deduce that the equation has at least two non-real roots.
parts.working: B1 Σα = 0, Σαβ = 1; B1 Σα² = −2; B1 a negative sum of squares means not all roots are real, and with real coefficients non-real roots come in conjugate pairs, so at least two.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of α³ + β³ + γ³ + δ³.
parts.working: M1 Σα³ = (Σα)³ − 3ΣαΣαβ + 3Σαβγ with Σαβγ = −2; A1 −6.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the value of α⁴ + β⁴ + γ⁴ + δ⁴.

check: (lambda a,b,c,d: a**2-2*b)(Fraction(0,1),Fraction(1,1),Fraction(-2,1),Fraction(6,1)) == Fraction(-2,1) and (lambda a,b,c,d: a**3-3*a*b+3*c)(Fraction(0,1),Fraction(1,1),Fraction(-2,1),Fraction(6,1)) == Fraction(-6,1) and -(-2) - 2*0 - 24 == -22
author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation x³ − 3x² + 5x − 2 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the cubic equation whose roots are 2α, 2β and 2γ.
parts.working: M1 substitute x = y/2: y³/8 − 3y²/4 + 5y/2 − 2 = 0; A1 multiply by 8: y³ − 6y² + 20y − 16 = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use your equation to find the value of 1/(2α) + 1/(2β) + 1/(2γ).
parts.working: M1 sum of reciprocals of new roots = 20/16; A1 5/4.

author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation 2x³ + x² − 4x + 3 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the equation whose roots are 1/α, 1/β and 1/γ is 3y³ − 4y² + y + 2 = 0.
parts.working: M1 substitute x = 1/y; A1 multiply through by y³: 2 + y − 4y² + 3y³ = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of 1/α² + 1/β² + 1/γ².
parts.working: M1 for the new equation Σ1/α = 4/3, Σ1/(αβ) = 1/3; M1 (4/3)² − 2(1/3); A1 10/9.

author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation x³ + 2x² − 3x + 1 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Using the substitution y = x − 1, find the cubic equation whose roots are α − 1, β − 1 and γ − 1.
parts.working: M1 substitute x = y + 1; M1 expand (y + 1)³ + 2(y + 1)² − 3(y + 1) + 1; A1 y³ + 5y² + 4y + 1 = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of (α − 1)(β − 1)(γ − 1) and of 1/(α − 1) + 1/(β − 1) + 1/(γ − 1).
parts.working: B1 product of new roots = −1; M1 sum of reciprocals = (sum of products in pairs)/(product) = 4/(−1); A1 −4.

author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation x³ − 4x² + x + 3 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Using the substitution y = x², show that the equation whose roots are α², β², γ² is y³ − 14y² + 25y − 9 = 0.
parts.working: M1 x³ + x = 4x² − 3, i.e. x(x² + 1) = 4x² − 3; M1 square both sides: x²(x² + 1)² = (4x² − 3)²; M1 replace x² by y: y(y + 1)² = (4y − 3)²; A1 y³ − 14y² + 25y − 9 = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of α⁴ + β⁴ + γ⁴.

author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation x³ + x² − 2x + 5 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why β + γ = −1 − α.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the cubic equation with roots β + γ, γ + α and α + β.
parts.working: M1 y = −1 − x, so substitute x = −1 − y; M1 expand (−1 − y)³ + (−1 − y)² − 2(−1 − y) + 5 = 0; A1 y³ + 2y² − y − 7 = 0.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence write down the value of (α + β)(β + γ)(γ + α).
parts.working: B1 product of roots of the new equation = 7.

author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation 3x³ − 2x² + x − 4 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that if y = x/(x + 1) then x = y/(1 − y).
parts.working: B1 y(x + 1) = x so x(1 − y) = y.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the cubic equation, with integer coefficients, whose roots are α/(α + 1), β/(β + 1) and γ/(γ + 1).
parts.working: M1 substitute x = y/(1 − y); M1 multiply by (1 − y)³: 3y³ − 2y²(1 − y) + y(1 − y)² − 4(1 − y)³ = 0; M1 expand; A1 10y³ − 16y² + 13y − 4 = 0.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence find the value of α/(α + 1) + β/(β + 1) + γ/(γ + 1).
parts.working: B1 sum of roots = 8/5.

author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation x³ − 2x + 4 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why αβ = −4/γ.
parts.working: B1 product of roots = −d/a = −4.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that the equation whose roots are αβ, βγ and γα is y³ + 2y² − 16 = 0.
parts.working: M1 the new roots are −4/x for each root x, so substitute x = −4/y; M1 −64/y³ + 8/y + 4 = 0; A1 multiply by y³/4: y³ + 2y² − 16 = 0.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence find the value of α²β² + β²γ² + γ²α².
parts.working: M1 Σu² = (Σu)² − 2Σuv with Σu = −2, Σuv = 0; A1 4.

author: HomiLabs

stem: The equation x³ + x − 3 = 0 has roots α, β and γ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that α³ = 3 − α.
parts.working: B1 α satisfies α³ + α − 3 = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the cubic equation whose roots are α³, β³ and γ³.
parts.working: M1 y = 3 − x, so substitute x = 3 − y; M1 (3 − y)³ + (3 − y) − 3 = 0; A1 y³ − 9y² + 28y − 27 = 0.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence find the value of α⁶ + β⁶ + γ⁶.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the general solution of the differential equation d²y/dx² − 5 dy/dx + 6y = 0.
parts.working: M1 auxiliary equation m² − 5m + 6 = 0; A1 m = 2, 3 and y = Ae²ˣ + Be³ˣ.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that y = 2 and dy/dx = 5 when x = 0, find the particular solution.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the general solution of d²y/dx² + 4 dy/dx + 13y = 0.
parts.working: M1 m² + 4m + 13 = 0; A1 m = −2 ± 3i; A1 y = e⁻²ˣ(A cos 3x + B sin 3x).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the particular solution for which y = 1 and dy/dx = 0 when x = 0.
parts.working: B1 A = 1; M1 differentiate: dy/dx at 0 = −2A + 3B = 0; A1 B = 2/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the general solution of the differential equation d²y/dx² + 6 dy/dx + 9y = 18.
parts.working: M1 m² + 6m + 9 = 0, repeated root m = −3; A1 complementary function (A + Bx)e⁻³ˣ; M1 particular integral y = k gives 9k = 18; A1 y = (A + Bx)e⁻³ˣ + 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the limit of y as x → ∞.
parts.working: B1 (A + Bx)e⁻³ˣ → 0 so y → 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the complementary function for the differential equation d²y/dx² − dy/dx − 2y = 4x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find a particular integral of the form y = px + q, and hence write down the general solution.
parts.working: M1 substitute: −p − 2(px + q) = 4x; A1 p = −2, q = 1; A1 general solution y = Ae²ˣ + Be⁻ˣ − 2x + 1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the particular solution of the differential equation d²y/dx² + 2 dy/dx + 5y = 10 cos x, given that y = 0 and dy/dx = 0 when x = 0.
parts.answer: y = e⁻ˣ(−2 cos 2x − (3/2) sin 2x) + 2 cos x + sin x
parts.working: M1 auxiliary equation m² + 2m + 5 = 0; A1 m = −1 ± 2i, CF e⁻ˣ(A cos 2x + B sin 2x); M1 PI p cos x + q sin x; M1 substitute and compare: 4p + 2q = 10, 4q − 2p = 0; A1 p = 2, q = 1; B1 general solution y = e⁻ˣ(A cos 2x + B sin 2x) + 2 cos x + sin x; M1 y(0) = 0: A + 2 = 0; A1 A = −2; M1 y′(0) = −A + 2B + 1 = 0; A1 B = −3/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The displacement x metres of a model boat on a wave tank at time t seconds satisfies d²x/dt² + 4x = 8t². Find the general solution.
parts.working: M1 m² + 4 = 0, m = ±2i; A1 CF A cos 2t + B sin 2t; M1 PI at² + bt + c: 2a + 4(at² + bt + c) = 8t²; A1 a = 2, b = 0, c = −1; A1 general solution.

parts.label: b
parts.text: When t = 0, x = 0 and dx/dt = 2. Find x in terms of t.
parts.working: M1 A − 1 = 0 so A = 1; M1 dx/dt = −2A sin 2t + 2B cos 2t + 4t, so 2B = 2; A1 B = 1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the particular solution of d²y/dx² − 3 dy/dx + 2y = 6e³ˣ for which y = 4 and dy/dx = 6 when x = 0.
parts.working: M1 m² − 3m + 2 = 0; A1 CF Aeˣ + Be²ˣ; M1 PI ke³ˣ: 9k − 9k + 2k = 6; A1 k = 3; M1 A + B + 3 = 4; M1 A + 2B + 9 = 6; A1 A = 5, B = −4; A1 final answer.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why a particular integral of d²y/dx² + dy/dx − 6y = 10e²ˣ cannot be of the form ke²ˣ.
parts.answer: e²ˣ is part of the complementary function (m = 2 is a root of the auxiliary equation).
parts.working: B1 auxiliary equation m² + m − 6 = 0 has root 2, so ke²ˣ gives zero on the left side.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Using a particular integral of the form kxe²ˣ, find the general solution.
parts.working: B1 CF Ae²ˣ + Be⁻³ˣ; M1 y = kxe²ˣ, y′ = ke²ˣ(1 + 2x), y″ = ke²ˣ(4 + 4x); M1 substitute: ke²ˣ(4 + 4x + 1 + 2x − 6x) = 10e²ˣ; A1 5k = 10, k = 2; A1 general solution.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the solution of 4 d²y/dx² + 4 dy/dx + y = 3x + 2 for which y = 0 and dy/dx = 0 when x = 0.
parts.working: M1 4m² + 4m + 1 = 0; A1 m = −1/2 repeated, CF (A + Bx)e^(−x/2); M1 PI px + q: 4p + px + q = 3x + 2; A1 p = 3, q = −10; M1 y(0) = 0 gives A = 10; M1 differentiate and use y′(0) = 0: B − A/2 + 3 = 0; A1 B = 2; A1 final answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that, for large positive x, the graph of y approaches a straight line, and state its equation.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that y = −x cos 3x is a particular integral of d²y/dx² + 9y = 6 sin 3x.
parts.working: M1 y′ = −cos 3x + 3x sin 3x; M1 y″ = 6 sin 3x + 9x cos 3x; A1 y″ + 9y = 6 sin 3x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the solution for which y = 0 and dy/dx = 1 when x = 0.
parts.working: B1 CF A cos 3x + B sin 3x; M1 y(0) = 0 gives A = 0; M1 y′(0) = 3B − 1 = 1; A1 B = 2/3.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Describe the behaviour of y as x becomes large.
parts.answer: y oscillates with amplitude that grows without bound (roughly proportional to x).
parts.working: B1 the term −x cos 3x dominates: oscillations of increasing amplitude.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variable x satisfies d²x/dt² + 2 dx/dt + 2x = 4e⁻ᵗ, with x = 0 and dx/dt = 1 when t = 0. Find x in terms of t.
parts.answer: x = e⁻ᵗ(4 − 4 cos t + sin t)
parts.working: M1 m² + 2m + 2 = 0; A1 m = −1 ± i, CF e⁻ᵗ(A cos t + B sin t); M1 PI ke⁻ᵗ: k − 2k + 2k = 4; A1 k = 4; M1 x(0) = 0: A + 4 = 0; A1 A = −4; M1 differentiate, dx/dt at 0 = −A + B − 4 = 1; A1 B = 1; A1 final answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact value of x when t = π, and give it correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find a particular integral of d²y/dx² − 4 dy/dx + 4y = 8x² of the form ax² + bx + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that kx²e²ˣ is a particular integral of d²y/dx² − 4 dy/dx + 4y = e²ˣ for a suitable constant k, and find k.
parts.working: M1 y′ = ke²ˣ(2x + 2x²), y″ = ke²ˣ(2 + 8x + 4x²); M1 substitute: ke²ˣ(2 + 8x + 4x² − 8x − 8x² + 4x²) = 2ke²ˣ; A1 k = 1/2.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence write down the general solution of d²y/dx² − 4 dy/dx + 4y = 8x² + e²ˣ.
parts.working: B1 CF (A + Bx)e²ˣ; B1 sum of both particular integrals.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the solution of d²y/dx² − 2 dy/dx + 5y = 10 cos x for which y = 0 and dy/dx = 0 when x = 0. Hence find the exact value of y when x = π/2.
parts.working: M1 m² − 2m + 5 = 0; A1 m = 1 ± 2i, CF eˣ(A cos 2x + B sin 2x); M1 PI p cos x + q sin x; M1 compare: 4p − 2q = 10, 2p + 4q = 0; A1 p = 2, q = −1; M1 y(0) = 0: A + 2 = 0, A = −2; M1 y′(0) = A + 2B − 1 = 0; A1 B = 3/2; A1 solution; M1 substitute x = π/2: cos π = −1, sin π = 0; A1 2e^(π/2) − 1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the solution of the differential equation dy/dx + 2y/x = 6x, for x > 0, given that y = 3 when x = 1. Give y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 integrating factor e^(∫2/x dx) = x²; A1 d(x²y)/dx = 6x³; M1 integrate: x²y = 3x⁴/2 + c; A1 correct; M1 use (1, 3): c = 3/2; A1 y = 3x²/2 + 3/(2x²).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the general solution of dy/dx + 3y = 6e²ˣ.
parts.working: B1 integrating factor e³ˣ; M1 d(ye³ˣ)/dx = 6e⁵ˣ; M1 integrate: ye³ˣ = (6/5)e⁵ˣ + c; A1 y = (6/5)e²ˣ + ce⁻³ˣ.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the particular solution for which y = 2 when x = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that an integrating factor for the differential equation dy/dx + y tan x = sec x, 0 ≤ x < π/2, is sec x.
parts.working: M1 e^(∫tan x dx) = e^(ln sec x); A1 = sec x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the solution for which y = 1 when x = 0.
parts.working: M1 d(y sec x)/dx = sec² x; A1 y sec x = tan x + c; M1 x = 0, y = 1 gives c = 1; A1 y = sin x + cos x.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the solution of x dy/dx + 3y = x² ln x, for x > 0, given that y = 0 when x = 1.
parts.working: M1 divide by x: dy/dx + 3y/x = x ln x; A1 integrating factor x³; M1 d(x³y)/dx = x⁴ ln x; M1 integrate by parts; A1 x³y = (x⁵/5) ln x − x⁵/25 + c; M1 use y(1) = 0; A1 c = 1/25; A1 final answer.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the solution of dy/dx + 2xy/(x² + 1) = 4x for which y = 3 when x = 0. Show that it can be written as y = x² + 1 + 2/(x² + 1).
parts.working: M1 integrating factor e^(ln(x² + 1)) = x² + 1; A1 d((x² + 1)y)/dx = 4x(x² + 1); M1 integrate: (x² + 1)y = x⁴ + 2x² + c; A1 correct; M1 y(0) = 3 gives c = 3; A1 y = (x⁴ + 2x² + 3)/(x² + 1); A1 = ((x² + 1)² + 2)/(x² + 1) = x² + 1 + 2/(x² + 1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: By writing u = x² + 1, find the least value of y, giving your answer in exact form.
parts.working: M1 y = u + 2/u with u ≥ 1; M1 dy/du = 1 − 2/u² = 0 gives u = √2 (≥ 1, so attainable); A1 least value √2 + 2/√2 = 2√2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the solution of dy/dx − 2y = e²ˣ cos x for which y = 1 when x = 0.
parts.working: B1 integrating factor e⁻²ˣ; M1 d(ye⁻²ˣ)/dx = cos x; A1 ye⁻²ˣ = sin x + c; M1 c = 1; A1 y = e²ˣ(sin x + 1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = π/2, correct to 3 significant figures.

check: (lambda Y: max([abs((1)*(Y(t+1e-4,A,B,C)-Y(t-1e-4,A,B,C))/(2*1e-4) + (-2)*Y(t,A,B,C) - (math.exp(2*t)*math.cos(t))) for (t,A,B,C) in [(0.3,0,0,0), (0.7,0,0,0), (1.2,0,0,0)]]) < 0.001 and abs(Y(0,0,0,0) - (1)) < 1e-5)((lambda x,A,B,C: math.exp(2*x)*(math.sin(x) + 1))) and abs(math.exp(math.pi)*(math.sin(math.pi/2)+1) - 46.3) < 0.05
author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy (x + 1) dy/dx + y = x(x + 1) for x ≥ 0, and y = 2 when x = 0. Find y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 recognise the left side as d((x + 1)y)/dx (or divide and use integrating factor x + 1); A1 d((x + 1)y)/dx = x² + x; M1 integrate: (x + 1)y = x³/3 + x²/2 + c; A1 correct; M1 c = 2; A1 y = (2x³ + 3x² + 12)/(6(x + 1)).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the solution of sin x dy/dx + 2y cos x = cos x, for 0 < x < π, given that y = 3 when x = π/6. Hence find the value of y when x = π/2.
parts.answer: y = 1/2 + (5/8) cosec² x; y = 9/8 when x = π/2
parts.working: M1 divide by sin x: dy/dx + 2y cot x = cot x; M1 integrating factor e^(2 ln sin x) = sin² x; A1 d(y sin² x)/dx = sin x cos x; M1 integrate: y sin² x = (1/2) sin² x + c; A1 correct; M1 use (π/6, 3): 3/4 = 1/8 + c, c = 5/8; A1 y = 1/2 + (5/8) cosec² x; A1 y(π/2) = 9/8.

stem: A tank initially holds 100 litres of pure water. Salt solution with concentration 0.2 kg per litre flows in at 3 litres per minute, and the well-mixed solution flows out at 2 litres per minute. The tank does not overflow during the time considered. The mass of salt in the tank after t minutes is S kg.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that dS/dt + 2S/(100 + t) = 0.6.
parts.working: M1 inflow 3 × 0.2 = 0.6 kg/min; volume at time t is 100 + t litres, outflow 2 × S/(100 + t); A1 rearrange to given form.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Solve the differential equation to find S in terms of t.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the mass of salt in the tank after 50 minutes, correct to 3 significant figures.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the solution of x dy/dx − y = x³eˣ, for x > 0, given that y = 2 when x = 1.
parts.working: M1 divide by x: dy/dx − y/x = x²eˣ; A1 integrating factor 1/x; M1 d(y/x)/dx = xeˣ; M1 integrate by parts: y/x = (x − 1)eˣ + c; A1 correct; M1 use (1, 2): c = 2; A1 y = x(x − 1)eˣ + 2x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact value of y when x = 2.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Show that dy/dx > 0 for all x > 0.
parts.working: M1 dy/dx = (x² + x − 1)eˣ + 2; M1 for x ≥ 0.62 (where x² + x − 1 ≥ 0) every term is non-negative and 2 > 0; A1 for 0 < x < 0.62, x² + x − 1 > −1 and eˣ < 1.86, so (x² + x − 1)eˣ > −1.86 and dy/dx > 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution y = vx to show that the differential equation dy/dx = (x² + y²)/(xy), x > 0, reduces to x dv/dx = 1/v.
parts.working: M1 dy/dx = v + x dv/dx; M1 right side = (1 + v²)/v = 1/v + v; A1 x dv/dx = 1/v.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find y² in terms of x, given that y = 2 when x = 1.
parts.working: M1 separate: v dv = dx/x; A1 v²/2 = ln x + c; M1 x = 1, v = 2: c = 2; A1 y² = 2x²(ln x + 2).

check: (lambda Y: max([abs((Y(t+1e-6)-Y(t-1e-6))/2e-6 - (t*t + Y(t)**2)/(t*Y(t))) for t in [0.8, 1.5, 2.7]]) < 1e-5 and abs(Y(1) - 2) < 1e-12)(lambda x: math.sqrt(2*x*x*(math.log(x)+2)))
author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the substitution x = eᵗ transforms the differential equation x² d²y/dx² − 3x dy/dx + 3y = 6 into d²y/dt² − 4 dy/dt + 3y = 6.
parts.working: M1 dy/dx = e⁻ᵗ dy/dt, so x dy/dx = dy/dt; M1 d²y/dx² = e⁻²ᵗ(d²y/dt² − dy/dt); A1 x² d²y/dx² = d²y/dt² − dy/dt; A1 substitute: d²y/dt² − dy/dt − 3 dy/dt + 3y = 6.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the general solution for y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 m² − 4m + 3 = 0, m = 1, 3; A1 CF Aeᵗ + Be³ᵗ; B1 PI y = 2; A1 y = Ax + Bx³ + 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the substitution z = 1/y transforms dy/dx + y/x = xy² into dz/dx − z/x = −x.
parts.working: M1 dy/dx = −(1/z²) dz/dx; M1 substitute: −(1/z²) dz/dx + 1/(xz) = x/z²; A1 multiply by −z²: dz/dx − z/x = −x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find y in terms of x, given that y = 1/2 when x = 1.
parts.working: M1 integrating factor 1/x; A1 d(z/x)/dx = −1; M1 z/x = −x + c; M1 z = 2 at x = 1 gives c = 3; A1 y = 1/(3x − x²).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the substitution y = u/x transforms the differential equation x d²y/dx² + 2 dy/dx + 4xy = 0 into d²u/dx² + 4u = 0.
parts.working: M1 dy/dx = u′/x − u/x²; M1 d²y/dx² = u″/x − 2u′/x² + 2u/x³; M1 substitute: (u″ − 2u′/x + 2u/x²) + (2u′/x − 2u/x²) + 4u; A1 u″ + 4u = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find y in terms of x, given that y = 2/π when x = π/4 and y = 0 when x = π/2.
parts.working: M1 u = A cos 2x + B sin 2x; A1 y = (A cos 2x + B sin 2x)/x; M1 x = π/2: −A/(π/2) = 0, A = 0; M1 x = π/4: B/(π/4) = 2/π; A1 B = 1/2, y = sin 2x/(2x).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the substitution u = y² transforms the differential equation dy/dx − y = xe²ˣ/y into du/dx − 2u = 2xe²ˣ.
parts.working: M1 du/dx = 2y dy/dx; M1 multiply the equation by 2y: 2y dy/dx − 2y² = 2xe²ˣ; A1 du/dx − 2u = 2xe²ˣ.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that y = 3 when x = 0 and y > 0, find y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 integrating factor e⁻²ˣ; A1 d(ue⁻²ˣ)/dx = 2x; M1 ue⁻²ˣ = x² + c; M1 u = 9 at x = 0, c = 9; A1 y² = (x² + 9)e²ˣ so y = eˣ√(x² + 9).

check: (lambda Y: max([abs((Y(t+1e-6)-Y(t-1e-6))/2e-6 - Y(t) - t*math.exp(2*t)/Y(t)) for t in [-0.5, 0.4, 1.1]]) < 1e-4 and Y(0) == 3)(lambda x: math.exp(x)*math.sqrt(x*x + 9))
author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: The displacement x of a damped oscillator at time t satisfies d²x/dt² + 3 dx/dt + 2x = 4 sin 2t. Find the general solution.
parts.working: M1 m² + 3m + 2 = 0; A1 CF Ae⁻ᵗ + Be⁻²ᵗ; M1 PI p cos 2t + q sin 2t; M1 compare: −2p + 6q = 0, −6p − 2q = 4; A1 p = −3/5, q = −1/5; A1 general solution.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe the motion for large values of t, and find the amplitude of this motion in exact form.
parts.answer: x ≈ −(3/5) cos 2t − (1/5) sin 2t: oscillation with period π and amplitude √10/5 ≈ 0.632
parts.working: M1 exponential terms → 0, so x approaches the particular integral; A1 oscillation of period π; A1 amplitude √((3/5)² + (1/5)²) = √10/5.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the solution of d²y/dx² + 2 dy/dx + 10y = 20 + 18e⁻ˣ for which y = 0 and dy/dx = 0 when x = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State what happens to y as x → ∞, and explain why the answer does not depend on the initial conditions.
parts.working: B1 y → 2; B1 every other term contains the factor e⁻ˣ, which tends to 0 whatever the values of the arbitrary constants.

topic: Linear motion under a variable force
stem: A particle P of mass 2 kg moves in a straight line on a smooth horizontal surface. The only horizontal force on P is a resistance of magnitude 4v N, where v m s⁻¹ is its speed. Initially P has speed 10 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that v = 10e⁻²ᵗ, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed of P at time t s.
parts.working: M1 Newton's second law: 2 dv/dt = −4v; M1 separate and integrate: ln v = −2t + c; A1 v = 10 at t = 0 gives v = 10e⁻²ᵗ.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken for the speed of P to fall to 2 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the distance travelled by P in this time.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Linear motion under a variable force
stem: An ice-hockey puck of mass 0.5 kg slides in a straight line across horizontal ice. Air resistance and friction together are modelled as a single resisting force of magnitude 0.1v² N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed. The puck starts with speed 20 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that v = 20e^(−0.2x), where v m s⁻¹ is the speed of the puck when it has travelled x m.
parts.working: M1 use acceleration v dv/dx: 0.5v dv/dx = −0.1v²; A1 dv/dx = −0.2v; M1 integrate: ln v = −0.2x + c; A1 v = 20 at x = 0 gives result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance travelled when the speed has fallen to 5 m s⁻¹.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Linear motion under a variable force
stem: A car of mass 800 kg starts from rest on a straight horizontal road. The engine produces a constant driving force of 2400 N and the resistance to motion is 40v N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed of the car after t seconds.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the greatest speed the car could approach under this model.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that v = 60(1 − e^(−t/20)).
parts.working: M1 800 dv/dt = 2400 − 40v; M1 separate: ∫ dv/(60 − v) = ∫ dt/20; A1 −ln(60 − v) = t/20 + c; A1 v = 0 at t = 0 gives result.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for the car to reach 30 m s⁻¹.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Linear motion under a variable force
stem: A small stone of mass 0.2 kg is released from rest and falls vertically through the air. The air resistance is 0.05v N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed after t s. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that dv/dt = 10 − 0.25v and hence find v in terms of t.
parts.working: M1 0.2 dv/dt = 0.2(10) − 0.05v; A1 dv/dt = 10 − 0.25v; M1 separate and integrate: −4 ln(40 − v) = t + c; A1 v = 40(1 − e^(−t/4)).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of the stone after 3 seconds.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the terminal speed of the stone.
parts.working: B1 v → 40 as t → ∞.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Linear motion under a variable force
stem: A cyclist and her bicycle have total mass 80 kg. She rides along a straight horizontal road in Islamabad, working at a constant power of 240 W. The resistance to motion is 2v N, where v m s⁻¹ is her speed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that 80v dv/dt = 240 − 2v².
parts.working: M1 driving force = power/speed = 240/v; A1 80 dv/dt = 240/v − 2v, multiply by v.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest speed that the cyclist can approach.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the cyclist when her speed is 5 m s⁻¹.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Linear motion under a variable force
stem: A particle P of mass 3 kg moves along the positive x-axis on a smooth horizontal surface. It passes through the origin O with speed 8 m s⁻¹ and is subject to a resisting force of magnitude 6v N, where v m s⁻¹ is its speed when its displacement from O is x m.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Using acceleration in the form v dv/dx, show that v = 8 − 2x.
parts.working: M1 3v dv/dx = −6v; A1 dv/dx = −2; A1 v = 8 − 2x using v = 8 at x = 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of x when v = 2, and explain why P never reaches the point where x = 4.
parts.working: B1 x = 3; M1 from 3 dv/dt = −6v, v = 8e⁻²ᵗ, which is never zero; A1 so x = 4 − 4e⁻²ᵗ < 4 for all t.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for P to travel from O to the point where x = 3.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Linear motion under a variable force
stem: A ball of mass 0.1 kg is projected vertically upwards with speed 15 m s⁻¹. Air resistance has magnitude 0.02v² N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed of the ball. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the greatest height above the point of projection reached by the ball.

parts.label: b

stem: A car of mass 1200 kg moves along a straight horizontal motorway between Lahore and Islamabad. Its engine works at a constant rate of 30 kW and the resistance to motion is 25v N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed.

parts.label: a

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the time taken for the block to come to rest.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance travelled by the block before it comes to rest.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b

stem: A particle of mass 5 kg is projected with speed 12 m s⁻¹ up a line of greatest slope of a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. Air resistance has magnitude 0.5v² N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a

parts.working: M1 5v dv/dx = −5g sin 30° − 0.5v²; A1 divide by 5: v dv/dx = −(5 + 0.1v²).

parts.text: Find the distance the particle travels up the plane before coming to instantaneous rest.

stem: A train of mass 50 000 kg starts from rest on a straight level track. The engine exerts a constant driving force of 40 000 N and the resistance to motion is kv N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed and k is a constant.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that the greatest speed the train can approach is 40 m s⁻¹, show that k = 1000.

topic: Linear motion under a variable force
stem: A particle of mass m kg is projected vertically upwards with speed 30 m s⁻¹. Air resistance has magnitude 0.01mv² N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed, and acts opposite to the direction of motion. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the greatest height reached above the point of projection.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of the particle when it returns to the point of projection.
parts.working: M1 downwards: v dv/dy = 10 − 0.01v², y measured down from the top; M1 H = −50 ln(1 − 0.001w²); M1 equate: 1/(1 − 0.001w²) = 1.9; A1 w² = 1000(1 − 1/1.9) = 473.7; A1 w = 21.8 m s⁻¹.

topic: Linear motion under a variable force

parts.label: c

stem: A sledge of mass 0.8 kg slides across smooth horizontal ice in a straight line. It passes the point O with speed 20 m s⁻¹, and air resistance has magnitude 0.04v² N, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed.

topic: Linear motion under a variable force
stem: A puck of mass m kg slides in a straight line on a rough horizontal floor, with coefficient of friction 0.2. In addition, air resistance of magnitude 0.1mv² N acts, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed. The initial speed is 10 m s⁻¹. Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the deceleration of the puck is (2 + 0.1v²) m s⁻².
parts.working: M1 friction μmg = 0.2 × 10 × m = 2m N; A1 total resisting force m(2 + 0.1v²), divide by m.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken for the puck to come to rest.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the distance travelled before it comes to rest.

stem: A particle P of mass 0.5 kg starts from rest at a point O and moves in a straight line on a smooth horizontal surface. At time t s it is acted on by a single horizontal force of magnitude 4e⁻ᵗ N in the direction of motion. Its speed is v m s⁻¹ and its displacement from O is x m.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find v in terms of t, and state the limiting value of v.
parts.working: M1 0.5 dv/dt = 4e⁻ᵗ; A1 v = −8e⁻ᵗ + c with v = 0 at t = 0, v = 8(1 − e⁻ᵗ); B1 v → 8.

stem: A particle of mass 3 kg moves in a straight line on a smooth horizontal surface under a single force of magnitude 12/(t + 1)² N, acting in the direction of motion, where t s is the time. At t = 0 its speed is 2 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that v = 6 − 4/(t + 1).
parts.working: M1 3 dv/dt = 12/(t + 1)²; A1 v = −4/(t + 1) + c; A1 v = 2 at t = 0 gives c = 6.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time at which the speed is 5 m s⁻¹, and the distance travelled up to that time.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Linear motion under a variable force
stem: A particle of mass 1 kg starts from rest and moves in a straight line on a horizontal surface. At time t s it is acted on by a force of magnitude 4t N in the direction of motion and a resistance of magnitude 2v N, where v m s⁻¹ is its speed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that dv/dt + 2v = 4t and hence find v in terms of t.
parts.working: B1 1 × dv/dt = 4t − 2v; M1 integrating factor e²ᵗ; M1 ve²ᵗ = ∫ 4te²ᵗ dt = (2t − 1)e²ᵗ + c; A1 c = 1 from v(0) = 0; A1 v = 2t − 1 + e⁻²ᵗ.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance travelled in the first 2 seconds.
parts.working: M1 v > 0 for t > 0, so distance = ∫₀² (2t − 1 + e⁻²ᵗ) dt; M1 [t² − t − e⁻²ᵗ/2]₀²; A1 2.5 − 0.5e⁻⁴ = 2.49 m.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Linear motion under a variable force
stem: A particle of mass 2 kg starts from rest at O and moves along a straight line on a smooth horizontal surface under a force of 6 sin 3t N, where t s is the time, acting along the line. Its velocity is v m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find v in terms of t.
parts.working: M1 2 dv/dt = 6 sin 3t; A1 v = −cos 3t + c; A1 c = 1.

parts.working: M1 differentiate again: e^(xy)(y + x y′)² + e^(xy)(2y′ + x y″) = y″; M1 substitute x = 0, y = 1, y′ = 0; A1 y″ = 1; A1 positive, so a minimum.

check: math.exp(0*1) == 0 + 1 and (lambda y, yp: math.exp(0)*(y + 0*yp)**2 + math.exp(0)*(2*yp))(1, 0) == 1

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has equation sin x + sin y = 1, for 0 < x < π/2, 0 < y < π/2. Find dy/dx at the point (π/6, π/6).
parts.working: M1 cos x + cos y(dy/dx) = 0; A1 dy/dx = −cos x/cos y = −1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that d²y/dx² at (π/6, π/6) is 2√3/3.
parts.working: M1 differentiate cos x + cos y·y′ = 0 again: −sin x − sin y·(y′)² + cos y·y″ = 0; M1 substitute values; A1 (√3/2)y″ = 1/2 + 1/2; A1 y″ = 2/√3 = 2√3/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has equation x² + xy + y² = 12. Find the coordinates of the points on C at which the tangent is parallel to the x-axis.
parts.working: M1 dy/dx = −(2x + y)/(x + 2y); M1 dy/dx = 0 gives y = −2x; M1 substitute: 3x² = 12; A1 (2, −4) and (−2, 4).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use d²y/dx² to determine the nature of each of these points.
parts.answer: (2, −4) is a minimum (d²y/dx² = 1/3); (−2, 4) is a maximum (d²y/dx² = −1/3)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the points on C at which the tangent is parallel to the y-axis.
parts.working: M1 x + 2y = 0; A1 both points.

check: 4 - 8 + 16 == 12 and Fraction(-2, 2 + 2*(-4)) == Fraction(1,3) and Fraction(-2, -2 + 2*4) == Fraction(-1,3) and 16 - 8 + 4 == 12
author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has equation x³ + y³ = 6xy. Find the exact coordinates of the point on C, other than the origin, at which the tangent is parallel to the x-axis.
parts.working: M1 3x² + 3y²(dy/dx) = 6y + 6x(dy/dx); A1 dy/dx = (2y − x²)/(y² − 2x); M1 dy/dx = 0 gives y = x²/2; M1 substitute: x³ + x⁶/8 = 3x³, x³ = 16; A1 x = 2∛2, y = 2∛4.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that at this point d²y/dx² = −1.
parts.working: M1 differentiate x² + y²y′ = 2y + 2xy′ again: 2x + 2y(y′)² + y²y″ = 4y′ + 2xy″; A1 with y′ = 0: y″ = −2x/(y² − 2x); A1 y² − 2x = 2^(10/3) − 2^(7/3) = 2^(7/3) = 2x, so y″ = −1 (a maximum).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has equation y³ + 3x²y = 4. Show that dy/dx = −2xy/(x² + y²).
parts.working: M1 3y²(dy/dx) + 6xy + 3x²(dy/dx) = 0; M1 collect terms; A1 result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find dy/dx and d²y/dx² at the point (1, 1), and describe what this suggests about the curve near this point.
parts.answer: dy/dx = −1, d²y/dx² = 0; the curve is approximately straight there (possible point of inflection)
parts.working: B1 dy/dx = −1; M1 differentiate (x² + y²)y′ = −2xy: (2x + 2y y′)y′ + (x² + y²)y″ = −2y − 2x y′; M1 substitute: (2 − 2)(−1) + 2y″ = −2 + 2; A1 y″ = 0, with comment.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve is defined parametrically by x = t² + 1, y = t³ − 3t. Find dy/dx in terms of t.
parts.working: M1 (dy/dt)/(dx/dt); A1 result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the stationary points of the curve.

parts.label: a
parts.text: An ellipse has parametric equations x = 2 cos θ, y = 3 sin θ. Find dy/dx in terms of θ.
parts.answer: dy/dx = −3 cos θ/(2 sin θ) = −(3/2) cot θ
parts.working: M1 dy/dθ = 3 cos θ, dx/dθ = −2 sin θ; A1 result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the ellipse at the point where θ = π/4, giving your answer in the form ax + by = c√2.
parts.working: M1 point (√2, 3√2/2); M1 gradient −3/2; A1 3x + 2y = 6√2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve has parametric equations x = 3t − 1, y = 2/t, t ≠ 0. Find dy/dx in terms of t.
parts.working: M1 dy/dt = −2/t², dx/dt = 3; A1 −2/(3t²).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the normal to the curve at the point where t = 1.
parts.working: B1 point (2, 2); M1 normal gradient 3/2; A1 y − 2 = (3/2)(x − 2), i.e. 2y = 3x − 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve has parametric equations x = t + 1/t, y = t − 1/t, t > 1. Show that dy/dx = (t² + 1)/(t² − 1).
parts.working: M1 dx/dt = 1 − 1/t², dy/dt = 1 + 1/t²; A1 multiply through by t².

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that d²y/dx² = −4t³/(t² − 1)³ and find its value when t = 2.
parts.working: M1 d/dt of dy/dx = −4t/(t² − 1)²; M1 divide by dx/dt = (t² − 1)/t²; A1 −4t³/(t² − 1)³; A1 −32/27.

check: (lambda t: Fraction(-4*t**3, (t*t - 1)**3) == Fraction(-32,27) and Fraction(-4*t, (t*t - 1)**2) / Fraction(t*t - 1, t*t) == Fraction(-32,27))(2)

parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve has parametric equations x = ln(1 + t²), y = 2 tan⁻¹ t, for t > 0. Show that dy/dx = 1/t.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find d²y/dx² in terms of t, and its value at the point where t = 1.
parts.working: M1 d/dt(1/t) = −1/t²; M1 divide by 2t/(1 + t²); A1 −(1 + t²)/(2t³) = −1 at t = 1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve has parametric equations x = eᵗ cos t, y = eᵗ sin t. Show that dy/dx = (sin t + cos t)/(cos t − sin t).
parts.working: M1 product rule for both; A1 eᵗ cancels.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that d²y/dx² = 2/(eᵗ(cos t − sin t)³) and find its value at t = 0.
parts.working: M1 quotient rule in t: numerator (cos t − sin t)² + (sin t + cos t)² = 2; A1 d/dt = 2/(cos t − sin t)²; M1 divide by eᵗ(cos t − sin t); A1 value 2 at t = 0.

parts.text: A curve has parametric equations x = t² + 2t, y = t³ − 12t. Find the values of t at the stationary points of the curve.

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: A cycloid traced by a point on the rim of a bicycle wheel of radius a has parametric equations x = a(θ − sin θ), y = a(1 − cos θ), for 0 < θ < 2π. Show that dy/dx = cot(θ/2).
parts.working: M1 dy/dx = sin θ/(1 − cos θ); M1 double-angle forms 2 sin(θ/2)cos(θ/2)/(2 sin²(θ/2)); A1 cot(θ/2).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that d²y/dx² = −1/(4a sin⁴(θ/2)), and deduce that d²y/dx² = −a/y².
parts.working: M1 d/dθ cot(θ/2) = −(1/2)cosec²(θ/2); M1 divide by a(1 − cos θ) = 2a sin²(θ/2); A1 −1/(4a sin⁴(θ/2)); A1 y = 2a sin²(θ/2) so y² = 4a² sin⁴(θ/2), giving −a/y².

parts.label: a

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that f(x) = sec x, show that f″(x) = 2 sec³x − sec x.
parts.working: M1 f′ = sec x tan x; M1 f″ = sec x tan²x + sec³x; A1 use tan²x = sec²x − 1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the Maclaurin series for sec x up to and including the term in x⁴.
parts.working: M1 f‴ = 6 sec³x tan x − sec x tan x, f‴(0) = 0; M1 f⁗ = 18 sec³x tan²x + 6 sec⁵x − sec x tan²x − sec³x, f⁗(0) = 5; A1 f(0) = 1, f″(0) = 1; A1 1 + x²/2 + 5x⁴/24.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the Maclaurin series for tan⁻¹(1 + x) up to and including the term in x³.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the Maclaurin series for eˣ√(1 + 2x) up to and including the term in x³.
parts.working: M1 √(1 + 2x) = 1 + x − x²/2 + x³/2 + … (or differentiate directly); M1 multiply by 1 + x + x²/2 + x³/6; A1 x term 2x; A1 x² term 1/2 + 1 − 1/2 = 1; A1 x³ term 1/2 − 1/2 + 1/2 + 1/6 = 2/3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use your series to estimate e^0.1 √1.2 correct to 6 decimal places, and find the percentage error of your estimate correct to 2 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given f(x) = ln(cos x), for −π/2 < x < π/2, find the Maclaurin series for f(x) up to and including the term in x⁴.
parts.working: M1 f′ = −tan x, f″ = −sec²x, f‴ = −2 sec²x tan x; M1 f⁗ = −4 sec²x tan²x − 2 sec⁴x; A1 f(0) = 0, f′(0) = 0, f″(0) = −1, f‴(0) = 0, f⁗(0) = −2; M1 Maclaurin formula; A1 −x²/2 − 2x⁴/24; A1 = −x²/2 − x⁴/12.

parts.label: b

parts.working: M1 tan x = −d/dx ln(cos x); A1 −(−x − x³/3) = x + x³/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that y = sin⁻¹x, show that (1 − x²)(d²y/dx²) − x(dy/dx) = 0.
parts.working: M1 dy/dx = (1 − x²)^(−1/2), so √(1 − x²)·dy/dx = 1; M1 differentiate: √(1 − x²)y″ − x(1 − x²)^(−1/2)y′ = 0; A1 multiply by √(1 − x²).

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find dy/dx when y = sinh⁻¹(3x).
parts.working: M1 chain rule with d/du sinh⁻¹u = 1/√(u² + 1); A1.

parts.working: B1

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: By writing x = cosh y, prove that d/dx (cosh⁻¹x) = 1/√(x² − 1), for x > 1.
parts.working: M1 dx/dy = sinh y; M1 sinh y = √(cosh²y − 1) = √(x² − 1) (positive since y > 0); A1 dy/dx = 1/√(x² − 1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the gradient of the curve y = x cosh⁻¹x at the point where x = 2, giving your answer in exact form and correct to 3 decimal places.
parts.working: M1 product rule: cosh⁻¹x + x/√(x² − 1); M1 cosh⁻¹2 = ln(2 + √3); A1 ln(2 + √3) + 2√3/3 = 2.472.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that d/dx [tan⁻¹(eˣ)] = (1/2) sech x.
parts.working: M1 chain rule: eˣ/(1 + e²ˣ); M1 divide numerator and denominator by eˣ: 1/(e⁻ˣ + eˣ); A1 = 1/(2 cosh x) = (1/2) sech x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of ∫₀^(ln 3) sech x dx.
parts.working: M1 ∫ sech x dx = 2 tan⁻¹(eˣ); M1 limits: 2 tan⁻¹3 − 2 tan⁻¹1; A1 2 tan⁻¹3 − π/2 ≈ 0.927.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform cuboid packing crate stands on rough horizontal ground. Its weight is 200 N, its height is 1.2 m and its square base has side 0.6 m. parts.working: M1 moments about the lower edge on the far side: P × 1.2 = 200 × 0.3; A1 equation; A1 P = 50.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The coefficient of friction between the crate and the ground is μ. Find the set of values of μ for which the crate tips over before it slides, as P is gradually increased.
parts.working: M1 sliding needs P > 200μ; M1 tipping first requires 50 < 200μ; A1 μ > 0.25.

parts.label: c

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform solid hemisphere of radius r rests in equilibrium with its curved surface in contact with a rough plane inclined at α to the horizontal. Show that the plane face of the hemisphere makes an angle θ with the horizontal, where sin θ = (8/3) sin α.

parts.label: b

parts.label: c

parts.working: B1 friction resolves along the plane: F = W sin α, R = W cos α, μ ≥ tan α.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform rectangular lamina OABC has vertices O(0, 0), A(8a, 0), B(8a, 4a) and C(0, 4a). The triangle with vertices A, B and P(6a, 2a) is removed. Find the coordinates of the centre of mass of the remaining lamina.

parts.label: b

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform ladder rests in limiting equilibrium with its foot on rough horizontal ground (coefficient of friction μ₁) and its top against a rough vertical wall (coefficient of friction μ₂). The ladder makes an angle θ with the ground. Show that tan θ = (1 − μ₁μ₂)/(2μ₁).

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: A uniform rod AB of weight W has end A on rough horizontal ground. The rod is held at 40° to the horizontal by a light string attached at B, the string being perpendicular to the rod and in the same vertical plane. Find the tension in the string in terms of W.

parts.label: b

parts.working: M1 moments about A; A1 P × 2a cos θ = W × a sin θ; A1 P = (W/2) tan θ.

parts.label: b

parts.label: a

parts.text:
A board-game club in Rawalpindi suspects that one of its dice is biased. The die is thrown 120 times with these results.
Score: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
Frequency: 15, 25, 18, 22, 16, 24
Test, at the 5% significance level, whether the die is fair.
parts.answer: X² = 4.50, ν = 5, critical value 11.07; 4.50 < 11.07, so do not reject H₀: there is insufficient evidence that the die is biased
parts.working: B1 H₀: the die is fair (each score has probability 1/6); H₁: the die is not fair; M1 each expected frequency 120/6 = 20; M1 X² = Σ(O − E)²/E = 4.50; B1 ν = 5, critical value 11.07; A1 4.50 < 11.07, so do not reject H₀: there is insufficient evidence that the die is biased.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A plant breeder crosses two varieties of pea. Genetic theory predicts the four types of offspring (round-yellow, round-green, wrinkled-yellow, wrinkled-green) in the ratio 9 : 3 : 3 : 1. parts.working: M1 160 × 9/16 etc.; A1 all four correct.

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text:
The head teacher of a school in Lahore records the number of student absences on each weekday over one term.
Day: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday
Absences: 50, 28, 26, 30, 46
Test, at the 5% significance level, whether absences are equally likely to occur on each weekday.
parts.answer: X² = 13.8, ν = 4, critical value 9.488; 13.8 > 9.488, so reject H₀: absences are not equally likely on each weekday
parts.working: B1 H₀: absences are uniformly distributed over the five days; H₁: they are not; M1 each expected frequency 180/5 = 36; M1 X² = Σ(O − E)²/E = 13.8; B1 ν = 4, critical value 9.488; A1 13.8 > 9.488, so reject H₀: absences are not equally likely on each weekday.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State which days contribute most to the value of the test statistic and suggest a reason in context.
parts.answer: Monday and Friday (O − E = 14 and 10, contributions 5.44 and 2.78); students may be extending their weekends
parts.working: B1 Monday and Friday identified with contributions; B1 sensible reason.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
A commuter in Karachi notes the number of minutes past the hour at which 120 buses arrived at a stop. The times are grouped into ten-minute intervals.
Minutes past the hour: 0–, 10–, 20–, 30–, 40–, 50–60
Frequency: 28, 16, 18, 22, 14, 22
Test, at the 10% significance level, whether the arrival time (in minutes past the hour) can be modelled by a continuous uniform distribution on [0, 60].
parts.answer: X² = 6.40, ν = 5, critical value 9.236; 6.40 < 9.236, so do not reject H₀: the uniform distribution is a suitable model
parts.working: B1 H₀: arrival time ~ U(0, 60); H₁: it does not follow this distribution; M1 each interval has probability 1/6, expected frequency 20; M1 X² = Σ(O − E)²/E = 6.40; B1 ν = 5, critical value 9.236; A1 6.40 < 9.236, so do not reject H₀: the uniform model is suitable.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A toy company asked 60 children in Islamabad to choose their favourite of four colours for a new toy: red, blue, green and yellow. The choices were 20, 14, 10 and 16 respectively. Test, at the 5% significance level, whether all four colours are equally popular.
parts.answer: X² = 3.47, ν = 3, critical value 7.815; 3.47 < 7.815, so do not reject H₀: there is insufficient evidence that the colours differ in popularity
parts.working: B1 H₀: the four colours are equally popular; H₁: they are not; M1 each expected frequency 15; M1 X² = Σ(O − E)²/E = 3.47; B1 ν = 3, critical value 7.815; A1 3.47 < 7.815, so do not reject H₀: insufficient evidence.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A larger survey of 180 children produced exactly the same proportions choosing each colour. Show that the test statistic is now three times as large and state the conclusion of the same test.
parts.answer: X² = 10.4 (= 3 × 3.47); 10.4 > 7.815, reject H₀: the colours are not equally popular
parts.working: M1 every O and E is multiplied by 3, so each (O − E)²/E is multiplied by 9/3 = 3; A1 X² = 10.4; A1 exceeds 7.815, conclusion reverses.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Comment on what this shows about the effect of sample size on a goodness-of-fit test.
parts.answer: Larger samples make the test more sensitive (more powerful): the same proportional discrepancy becomes significant

parts.label: a
parts.text: A garden designer in Islamabad models the edge of a flower bed by the curve r = 2 + sin θ, for 0 ≤ θ < 2π, where r is in metres. Show that r > 0 for all θ and state the greatest and least values of r.
parts.working: B1 since −1 ≤ sin θ ≤ 1, 1 ≤ r ≤ 3 so r > 0; B1 both values with θ.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact area of the flower bed.
parts.working: M1 ½∫(4 + 4sin θ + sin²θ) dθ; M1 sin²θ = ½(1 − cos 2θ); M1 [4θ − 4cos θ + ½θ − ¼sin 2θ] from 0 to 2π = 9π; A1 9π/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = 1 + tan θ, for 0 ≤ θ ≤ ¼π. Show that r² = sec²θ + 2tan θ.
parts.working: B1 (1 + tan θ)² = 1 + tan²θ + 2tan θ = sec²θ + 2tan θ (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact area of the region bounded by C, the initial line and the half-line θ = ¼π. Give your answer in the form a + b ln 2.
parts.working: M1 ½∫(sec²θ + 2tan θ) dθ; A1 [tan θ + 2ln sec θ]; M1 limits: 1 + 2ln √2 = 1 + ln 2; A1 ½(1 + ln 2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = 2sin θ √(cos θ), for 0 ≤ θ ≤ ½π. Use the substitution u = sin θ to find the exact area of the region enclosed by C.
parts.working: M1 area = ½∫4sin²θ cos θ dθ; M1 du = cos θ dθ, limits 0 to 1; M1 2∫u² du = [2u³/3]; A1 2/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curves C₁ and C₂ have polar equations r = 3cos θ and r = 1 + cos θ respectively, for −½π ≤ θ ≤ ½π. Find the polar coordinates of the points of intersection of C₁ and C₂, other than the pole.
parts.working: M1 3cos θ = 1 + cos θ gives cos θ = ½; A1 both points.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact area of the region that is inside C₁ and outside C₂.
parts.working: M1 area = 2 × ½∫[9cos²θ − (1 + cos θ)²] dθ from 0 to π/3; M1 integrand 3 + 4cos 2θ − 2cos θ; A1 [3θ + 2sin 2θ − 2sin θ]; M1 limits: π + √3 − √3; A1 π.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The circles C₁ and C₂ have polar equations r = 4sin θ and r = 4cos θ, for 0 ≤ θ ≤ ½π. Find the polar coordinates of the point, other than the pole, where they meet.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact area of the region common to the interiors of both circles.
parts.working: M1 by symmetry area = 2 × ½∫16 sin²θ dθ from 0 to ¼π; M1 = 8∫(1 − cos 2θ) dθ; A1 [8θ − 4sin 2θ]; M1 limits 2π − 4; A1 2π − 4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = k(2 + cos θ), for 0 ≤ θ < 2π, where k is a positive constant. Show that the area enclosed by C is 9πk²/2.
parts.working: M1 ½k²∫(4 + 4cos θ + cos²θ) dθ; M1 cos²θ = ½(1 + cos 2θ); A1 integral over [0, 2π] = 8π + π = 9π; A1 9πk²/2 (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The area enclosed by C is 36π. Find the exact value of k and the greatest distance of a point on C from the pole.
parts.working: M1 9πk²/2 = 36π; A1 k² = 8, k = 2√2; B1 r max = 3k = 6√2 at θ = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = (1 + cos θ)√(sin θ), for 0 ≤ θ ≤ π. Show that the area of the region enclosed by C is 4/3.
parts.working: M1 ½∫(1 + cos θ)² sin θ dθ; M1 substitution u = 1 + cos θ, du = −sin θ dθ, limits 2 → 0; A1 ½∫u² du from 0 to 2; M1 ½[u³/3]; A1 4/3 (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of θ, for 0 < θ < π, at which r = 0 other than at the end points, or show that there is none.
parts.answer: None: r = 0 only when θ = 0 or θ = π
parts.working: B1 sin θ > 0 and 1 + cos θ > 0 for 0 < θ < π.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r² = 9cos 2θ. It consists of two loops, one for −¼π ≤ θ ≤ ¼π and one for ¾π ≤ θ ≤ 5π/4. Show that the total area enclosed by C is 9.
parts.working: M1 one loop = ½∫9cos 2θ dθ from −¼π to ¼π; A1 = 9/2; A1 total 9 (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The circle D has polar equation r = 3/√2. Find the values of θ in −¼π ≤ θ ≤ ¼π at which D meets C.
parts.working: M1 9cos 2θ = 9/2; A1 cos 2θ = ½, θ = ±π/6.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the exact total area of the parts of the region enclosed by C that lie outside D. Give the answer correct to 3 significant figures as well.
parts.working: M1 one loop: ½∫(9cos 2θ − 9/2) dθ from −π/6 to π/6; A1 [9/4 sin 2θ − 9θ/4] gives 9√3/4 − 3π/4; M1 double for two loops; A1 9√3/2 − 3π/2 = 3.08.

check: abs(2*2*((9/4)*math.sin(math.pi/3) - 9*(math.pi/6)/4) - (9*math.sqrt(3)/2 - 3*math.pi/2)) < 1e-9 and abs(9*math.sqrt(3)/2 - 3*math.pi/2 - 3.08) < 0.005 and abs(0.5*9*(math.sin(math.pi/2) - math.sin(-math.pi/2))/2 - 4.5) < 1e-9
author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = 3 sin 2θ, for 0 ≤ θ ≤ ½π. Find the polar coordinates of the point of C that is furthest from the pole.
parts.working: M1 sin 2θ = 1 or dr/dθ = 6cos 2θ = 0; A1 θ = ¼π, r = 3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the equations of the tangents to C at the pole.
parts.working: M1 r = 0 when sin 2θ = 0; A1 both.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = 4(1 + cos θ), for 0 ≤ θ ≤ π. Show that, at a point of C where the tangent is parallel to the initial line, 2cos²θ + cos θ − 1 = 0.
parts.working: M1 y = r sin θ = 4sin θ + 2sin 2θ; M1 dy/dθ = 4cos θ + 4cos 2θ = 0; A1 2cos²θ + cos θ − 1 = 0 (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the polar coordinates of this point, for 0 < θ < π, and its exact distance from the initial line.
parts.working: M1 (2cos θ − 1)(cos θ + 1) = 0, cos θ = ½; A1 θ = π/3, r = 6; A1 6 sin(π/3) = 3√3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = 2(1 − cos θ), for 0 ≤ θ ≤ π. Find the polar coordinates of the point of C, with 0 < θ < π, at which the tangent is perpendicular to the initial line.
parts.working: M1 x = r cos θ = 2cos θ − 2cos²θ; M1 dx/dθ = −2sin θ + 4sin θ cos θ = 2sin θ(2cos θ − 1); M1 = 0 with sin θ ≠ 0 so cos θ = ½; A1 θ = π/3, r = 1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = θ sin θ, for 0 ≤ θ ≤ π. Show that, at the point of C furthest from the pole, tan θ + θ = 0.
parts.working: M1 dr/dθ = sin θ + θ cos θ = 0; A1 divide by cos θ: tan θ + θ = 0 (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Verify that this equation has a root between 2 and 2.1.
parts.working: M1 evaluate at both ends; A1 change of sign (continuous on [2, 2.1]) so a root.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Given that the root is θ = 2.029 correct to 3 decimal places, find the greatest distance of a point on C from the pole, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 r = θ sin θ at θ = 2.029; A1 1.82.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = 3 + 2cos θ, for 0 ≤ θ ≤ π. Show that at the point P of C furthest from the initial line, 4cos²θ + 3cos θ − 2 = 0.
parts.working: M1 y = 3sin θ + 2sin θ cos θ = 3sin θ + sin 2θ; M1 dy/dθ = 3cos θ + 2cos 2θ = 0; A1 3cos θ + 4cos²θ − 2 = 0 (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the polar coordinates of P and its distance from the initial line, giving values correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 cos θ = (−3 + √41)/8 = 0.4254 (reject negative root < −1); A1 θ = 1.13; A1 r = 3.85; A1 r sin θ = 3.48.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = 1 + 2cos θ, for 0 ≤ θ ≤ ⅔π. State the equation of the tangent to C at the pole.
parts.working: B1 r = 0 when cos θ = −½.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that at the point of C furthest from the initial line, 4cos²θ + cos θ − 2 = 0.
parts.working: M1 y = sin θ + sin 2θ; M1 dy/dθ = cos θ + 2cos 2θ = 0; A1 4cos²θ + cos θ − 2 = 0 (AG).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence find this greatest distance from the initial line, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = 1 + θ, for 0 ≤ θ ≤ π. Show that the point of C furthest from the initial line satisfies tan θ = −(1 + θ).
parts.working: M1 y = (1 + θ)sin θ; M1 dy/dθ = sin θ + (1 + θ)cos θ = 0; A1 divide by cos θ (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Verify that this equation has a root α between 1.9 and 1.95.
parts.working: M1 values at both ends; A1 sign change, f continuous on the interval.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Use α = 1.903 to find the greatest distance of a point of C from the initial line, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = a + cos θ, for 0 ≤ θ ≤ π, where a is a positive constant. Show that dx/dθ = −sin θ(a + 2cos θ), where x = r cos θ.
parts.working: M1 x = a cos θ + cos²θ; A1 dx/dθ = −a sin θ − 2sin θ cos θ (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the set of values of a for which C has a point with 0 < θ < π at which the tangent is perpendicular to the initial line.
parts.working: M1 need cos θ = −a/2 with −1 < cos θ < 1; A1 0 < a < 2.

parts.label: c
parts.text: For a = 1, find the polar coordinates of this point.
parts.working: M1 cos θ = −½, θ = ⅔π; A1 r = 1 − ½ = ½.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = 4 sin θ cos²θ, for 0 ≤ θ ≤ ½π. Show that the greatest value of r occurs where tan²θ = ½.
parts.working: M1 dr/dθ = 4(cos³θ − 2sin²θ cos θ); M1 = 4cos θ(cos²θ − 2sin²θ) = 0; A1 cos θ ≠ 0 at a maximum inside the range, so tan²θ = ½ (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact greatest value of r, and the value of θ at which it occurs correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = 2(1 − cos θ), for 0 ≤ θ < 2π. Copy and complete the table of values: θ = 0, ½π, π, 3π/2.
parts.working: B1 two correct; B1 all four.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Sketch C, labelling the points where it crosses the initial line and the line θ = ½π. Describe its symmetry and its shape at the pole.
parts.answer: Cardioid, symmetric about the initial line, with a cusp at the pole pointing along θ = 0; passes through (2, ½π), (4, π), (2, 3π/2)
parts.working: B1 closed heart shape with r largest (4) at θ = π; B1 symmetry about the initial line; B1 cusp at the pole, tangent θ = 0.

check: [2*(1-math.cos(t)) for t in [0, math.pi/2, math.pi, 3*math.pi/2]] == [0, 2*(1-math.cos(math.pi/2)), 4, 2*(1-math.cos(3*math.pi/2))] and abs(2*(1-math.cos(math.pi/2)) - 2) < 1e-12
author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Sketch the spiral r = 3θ for 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π, marking the polar coordinates of the points where it meets the lines θ = ½π, θ = π and θ = 2π.
parts.answer: (3π/2, ½π), (3π, π), (6π, 2π); r increases steadily from 0
parts.working: B1 spiral starting at the pole, tangent θ = 0 there; B1 r increasing with θ, going anticlockwise; B1 three points correct.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the distance between the two points where the spiral crosses the initial line (including the pole).
parts.working: B1 r = 0 at θ = 0 and r = 6π at θ = 2π.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = 2cos 3θ, where r ≥ 0. Find the intervals of θ in 0 ≤ θ < 2π for which r ≥ 0.
parts.working: M1 cos 3θ ≥ 0 when 3θ in [0, π/2], [3π/2, 5π/2], …; A1 at least two intervals; A1 all.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Sketch C, stating the greatest value of r and the directions of the lines of symmetry of its loops.
parts.answer: Three equal loops (petals), r max = 2 along θ = 0, ⅔π, 4π/3; tangents at the pole θ = π/6, π/2, 5π/6, 7π/6, 3π/2, 11π/6
parts.working: B1 three loops; B1 tips at distance 2 along θ = 0, ⅔π, 4π/3; B1 loops meet only at the pole with correct tangents.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = 4cos 2θ, for −¼π ≤ θ ≤ ¼π and ¾π ≤ θ ≤ 5π/4. Show that r ≥ 0 throughout these intervals and find the tangents to C at the pole.
parts.working: B1 2θ lies in [−½π, ½π] or [3π/2, 5π/2] so cos 2θ ≥ 0; M1 r = 0 when cos 2θ = 0; A1 θ = ±¼π, ¾π, 5π/4.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Sketch C and state the polar coordinates of the points of C furthest from the pole.
parts.answer: Two loops along the initial line, tips at (4, 0) and (4, π)
parts.working: B1 two loops through the pole, symmetric about the initial line; B1 correct tangents at the pole; B1 (4, 0) and (4, π).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = 2 + cos 2θ, for 0 ≤ θ < 2π. Find the greatest and least values of r and the values of θ where they occur.
parts.answer: Greatest 3 at θ = 0, π; least 1 at θ = ½π, 3π/2
parts.working: M1 dr/dθ = −2sin 2θ = 0; A1 r = 3 at θ = 0, π; A1 r = 1 at θ = ½π, 3π/2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that C is symmetric about both the initial line and the line θ = ½π.
parts.working: B1 replacing θ by −θ leaves r unchanged; B1 replacing θ by π − θ leaves r unchanged.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Sketch C.
parts.answer: Closed curve not passing through the pole: r = 3 on the initial line (θ = 0, π) and r = 1 on θ = ½π, 3π/2; it is pinched in (concave, a 'peanut' shape) where it crosses θ = ½π and θ = 3π/2, and symmetric about both lines
parts.working: B1 closed curve, r > 0 throughout, with correct extremes 3 and 1 on the correct lines; B1 both symmetries shown and the curve dented inwards (not oval) near θ = ½π and 3π/2.

parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = 1 − 2cos θ, where r ≥ 0 and 0 ≤ θ < 2π. Find the range of values of θ for which r ≥ 0.
parts.working: M1 cos θ ≤ ½; A1 π/3 ≤ θ ≤ 5π/3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest value of r and sketch C, stating the equations of the tangents at the pole.

parts.working: B1 r max = 3 at θ = π; B1 tangents θ = π/3, 5π/3; B1 closed loop through the pole, lying mainly to the left of the pole; B1 symmetric about the initial line.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r = 4cos θ + 2sin θ. Find the Cartesian equation of C.
parts.working: M1 multiply by r: r² = 4r cos θ + 2r sin θ; A1 x² + y² = 4x + 2y.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that C is a circle and state its centre and radius.
parts.working: M1 (x − 2)² + (y − 1)² = 5; A1 centre and radius.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve C has polar equation r(1 − cos θ) = 2. Show that the Cartesian equation of C is y² = 4x + 4.
parts.working: M1 r = 2 + r cos θ = 2 + x; M1 x² + y² = (2 + x)²; A1 y² = 4x + 4 (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the polar coordinates of the point of C that is closest to the pole.
parts.working: M1 r = 2/(1 − cos θ) least when cos θ = −1; A1 r = 1, θ = π (the point (−1, 0)).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve has Cartesian equation (x² + y²)² = 4xy. Show that its polar equation is r² = 2sin 2θ.
parts.working: M1 r⁴ = 4r² cos θ sin θ; A1 r² = 2sin 2θ (AG).

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the values of θ, for 0 ≤ θ < 2π, for which the curve exists, and find the total area it encloses.
parts.answer: 0 ≤ θ ≤ ½π and π ≤ θ ≤ 3π/2; total area 2
parts.working: B1 sin 2θ ≥ 0 intervals; M1 one loop ½∫2sin 2θ dθ from 0 to ½π; A1 = 1; A1 total 2.

parts.working: M1 (cos θ + i sin θ)³ = cos 3θ + i sin 3θ; M1 expand, imaginary part 3cos²θ sin θ − sin³θ; M1 cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ; A1 3sin θ − 4sin³θ (AG).

parts.text: By writing z = cos θ + i sin θ and using z + 1/z = 2cos θ, show that cos⁴θ = ⅛(cos 4θ + 4cos 2θ + 3).
parts.working: M1 (z + 1/z)⁴ = 16cos⁴θ; M1 expand: z⁴ + z⁻⁴ + 4(z² + z⁻²) + 6; M1 zⁿ + z⁻ⁿ = 2cos nθ; A1 result (AG).

parts.working: M1 [⅛(¼sin 4θ + 2sin 2θ + 3θ)]; M1 limits; A1 ⅛(2 + 3π/4) = ¼ + 3π/32.

parts.text: Use de Moivre's theorem to show that tan 3θ = (3t − t³)/(1 − 3t²), where t = tan θ.
parts.working: M1 cos 3θ = c³ − 3cs², sin 3θ = 3c²s − s³; M1 divide; M1 by c³; A1 (AG).

parts.text: Using z = cos θ + i sin θ and z − 1/z = 2i sin θ, show that sin⁵θ = (1/16)(sin 5θ − 5sin 3θ + 10sin θ).
parts.working: M1 (z − 1/z)⁵ = 32i sin⁵θ; M1 expand: (z⁵ − z⁻⁵) − 5(z³ − z⁻³) + 10(z − z⁻¹); M1 zⁿ − z⁻ⁿ = 2i sin nθ; A1 32i sin⁵θ = 2i(sin 5θ − 5sin 3θ + 10sin θ); A1 (AG).

parts.text: Find the smallest positive integer n for which (√3 + i)ⁿ is a negative real number, and state the value of (√3 + i)ⁿ for this n.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use de Moivre's theorem to show that sin 6θ / sin θ = 32cos⁵θ − 32cos³θ + 6cos θ, for sin θ ≠ 0.
parts.working: M1 Im(c + is)⁶ = 6c⁵s − 20c³s³ + 6cs⁵; M1 divide by s; M1 s² = 1 − c², s⁴ = (1 − c²)²; M1 expand; A1 collect: 6c⁵ − 20c³ + 20c⁵ + 6c − 12c³ + 6c⁵; A1 32c⁵ − 32c³ + 6c (AG).

6.8, 7.9, 8.4, 7.1, 8.4, 9.2, 6.5, 8.7, 7.6, 9.0, 8.1, 7.4
Use a Wilcoxon signed-rank test at the 2.5% significance level to test her belief. (Give tied absolute differences the mean of their ranks.)
parts.answer: T = 20; critical value 13; do not reject H₀: insufficient evidence that the median pH exceeds 7.5
parts.working: B1 H₀: median = 7.5, H₁: median > 7.5; M1 differences from 7.5; M1 ranks with ties averaged: 0.1→1.5, −0.1→1.5, 0.4→3.5, −0.4→3.5, 0.6→5, −0.7→6, 0.9→7.5, 0.9→7.5, −1→9, 1.2→10, 1.5→11, 1.7→12; A1 P = 58; A1 Q = 20, T = 20; B1 critical value for n = 12 at 2.5% one-tailed: 13; M1 comparison; A1 conclusion in context.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A Wilcoxon signed-rank test compares the times taken by 30 delivery riders in Lahore to complete a route using an old map app and a new one (old time − new time). There are no zero differences. The sum of the ranks of the positive differences is 314. Using a suitable normal approximation, test at the 5% significance level whether the new app reduces the median time.
parts.answer: T = 151; z = −1.666; reject H₀: evidence that the new app reduces median time
parts.working: B1 H₀: median difference 0, H₁: median difference > 0; M1 Q = 465 − 314 = 151, T = 151; B1 E(T) = 30 × 31/4 = 232.5, Var(T) = 30 × 31 × 61/24 = 2363.75; M1 z = (151 + 0.5 − 232.5)/√2363.75 with continuity correction; A1 z = −1.666; M1 compare with −1.645; A1 reject H₀; evidence that the new app reduces median time.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
A phone maker claims that the median battery life of its new model under a standard test is 20 hours. A consumer group in Dubai tests 14 phones and records (hours):
18.6, 21.4, 17.9, 19.2, 16.8, 20.3, 18.1, 15.7, 19.6, 17.4, 16.2, 18.9, 20.8, 17.1
Test, at the 1% significance level, whether the median battery life is less than claimed.
parts.answer: T = 11; critical value 15; reject H₀: evidence that the median is less than 20 hours
parts.working: B1 H₀: median = 20, H₁: median < 20; M1 differences from 20; M1 ranks: 0.3→1, −0.4→2, −0.8→3.5, 0.8→3.5, −1.1→5, −1.4→6.5, 1.4→6.5, −1.9→8, −2.1→9, −2.6→10, −2.9→11, −3.2→12, −3.8→13, −4.3→14; A1 P = 11, Q = 94; A1 T = 11; B1 1% one-tailed critical value for n = 14: 15; A1 reject H₀; strong evidence that the median battery life is below 20 hours.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
An agricultural station near Multan divides each of 9 fields into two halves. One half is sown with wheat variety X and the other with variety Y. The yields (tonnes per hectare) are:
Field: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9
X: 3.42, 2.98, 3.75, 3.10, 3.56, 2.87, 3.33, 3.64, 3.05
Y: 3.51, 3.12, 3.69, 3.30, 3.71, 3.04, 3.29, 3.88, 3.27
Test at the 10% significance level whether there is a difference between the median yields of the two varieties.
parts.answer: T = 3; critical value 8; reject H₀: evidence of a difference
parts.working: B1 H₀: median difference = 0, H₁: ≠ 0; M1 differences X − Y; M1 ranks: 0.04→1, 0.06→2, −0.09→3, −0.14→4, −0.15→5, −0.17→6, −0.2→7, −0.22→8, −0.24→9; A1 P = 3, Q = 42; A1 T = 3; B1 two-tailed 10% critical value for n = 9: 8; A1 reject H₀; evidence of a difference in median yields.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why a paired test is appropriate here.
parts.answer: Each field gives a natural pair, removing differences between fields (soil, water)
parts.working: B1 same field for both varieties, so field-to-field variation is controlled.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In a Wilcoxon signed-rank test with 15 non-zero differences, P denotes the sum of the ranks of the positive differences. Find the set of values of P for which H₀: median difference = 0 is rejected in favour of H₁: median difference ≠ 0 at the 5% significance level.
parts.working: B1 P + Q = 120; B1 critical value 25; M1 reject when min(P, 120 − P) ≤ 25; A1 P ≤ 25 or P ≥ 95.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The experimenter actually obtains P = 96. One difference, with rank 7, was later found to have been recorded with the wrong sign: it should have been negative, not positive. Determine whether the conclusion of the test changes.
parts.answer: Yes: corrected P = 89, so H₀ is no longer rejected
parts.working: M1 corrected P = 96 − 7 = 89, Q = 31; A1 T = 31 > 25; A1 originally T = 24 ≤ 25 (reject), now do not reject: conclusion changes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A Wilcoxon signed-rank test is to be carried out on 40 non-zero paired differences, using a one-tailed test at the 1% significance level and a normal approximation with continuity correction. State the mean and variance of the test statistic T under H₀.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the largest value of T that leads to rejection of H₀.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
A Wilcoxon signed-rank test is used to test H₀: median = 12 against H₁: median ≠ 12 for the data
12.4, 15.1, 11.2, 13.8, 10.6, 14.3, 9.9
Show that, for these 7 values, P = 18 and Q = 10, and carry out the test at the 5% significance level.
parts.answer: T = 10; critical value 2; do not reject H₀

parts.label: b
parts.text: An eighth value x is added, where x > 16. Find the new value of T and determine whether the conclusion changes.
parts.answer: T = 10; critical value 3; conclusion unchanged: do not reject H₀
parts.working: M1 x − 12 > 4 has the largest absolute difference, rank 8, others keep their ranks; A1 P = 26, Q = 10, T = 10; A1 critical value for n = 8 is 3: do not reject H₀; conclusion unchanged.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Seven students in Kuala Lumpur sit a mental-arithmetic quiz, then practise for a week and sit a similar quiz. Their scores are:
First quiz: 64, 71, 58, 80, 67, 75, 62
Second quiz: 70, 74, 57, 88, 73, 84, 68
State suitable hypotheses for a test of whether practice increases the median score.
parts.answer: H₀: median of (second − first) = 0; H₁: median of (second − first) > 0
parts.working: B1 both, in terms of the population median difference.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Carry out a Wilcoxon signed-rank test at the 5% significance level.
parts.answer: T = 1; critical value 3; reject H₀: evidence that practice increases the median score
parts.working: M1 differences (second − first): 6, 3, −1, 8, 6, 9, 6; M1 ranks: −1→1, 3→2, 6→4, 6→4, 6→4, 8→6, 9→7; A1 P = 27, Q = 1, T = 1; B1 critical value 3; A1 conclusion in context.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Two examiners each mark the same 14 essays out of 100.
Examiner 1: 56, 72, 64, 81, 49, 68, 77, 59, 85, 62, 70, 53, 66, 74
Examiner 2: 61, 70, 71, 84, 57, 66, 83, 68, 86, 70, 79, 50, 75, 78
Use a Wilcoxon signed-rank test at the 2% significance level to test whether there is a difference between the examiners' median marks. Use the mean rank for tied values.
parts.answer: T = 9.5; critical value 15; reject H₀: evidence of a difference between the examiners
parts.working: B1 H₀: median difference = 0, H₁: ≠ 0; M1 differences (E1 − E2); M1 ranks with ties: −1→1, 2→2.5, 2→2.5, −3→4.5, 3→4.5, −4→6, −5→7, −6→8, −7→9, −8→10.5, −8→10.5, −9→13, −9→13, −9→13; A1 P = 9.5; A1 Q = 95.5; B1 2% two-tailed critical value for n = 14 is 15; M1 T = 9.5 compared; A1 reject H₀; evidence that the examiners differ (examiner 2 tends to mark higher).
